newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court serves arrest warrant on E. German leader.
newsitem.headline: Court serves arrest warrant on E. German leader.

text.p: A Berlin court on Thursday served arrest warrants on East Germany's last hardline communist leader Egon Krenz and three of his deputies after a higher court ruled that they could be jailed if convicted of manslaughter.
The four East German leaders have been on trial for the last year, charged with responsibility for deaths at the Berlin Wall and the fortified border between the former two Germanys.

The long-awaited ruling by the supreme court in Karlsruhe on Tuesday allowed former East German leaders to be jailed for the "shoot to kill" orders during the Cold War and removed an important line of defence Krenz had been using in the trial. A Berlin state justice ministry spokesman said Krenz and his former colleagues -- Guenter Schabowski, Guenther Kleiber and Horst Dohlus -- would not be immediately imprisoned as a result of the warrants but they would have to give up their passports.

The spokesman, Ruediger Reiff, said Krenz, Klieber and Dohlus would not be allowed to leave Berlin or the surrounding area while Schabowski would be permitted to travel to his place of work in central Germany.
The four men will be required to report to the police regularly for the duration of the court proceedings.

One East German already convicted for his part in the border killings, Klaus-Dieter Baumgarten, was quickly arrested on Wednesday in Berlin. The border guard chief had not been jailed pending the supreme court ruling.
Krenz blasted the ruling on Wednesday in an interview with Reuters and said it was more likely he would end up behind bars.
The 59-year-old led East Germany for just three weeks in 1989 after longtime leader Erich Honecker quit.
